lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - A Look & write

details: Look and write serves as a comprehensive review of the unit's language. Students must use the visual and text clues to write the correct past tense activity phrases, consolidating vocabulary and grammar.
Look for correctly written past tense phrases that logically fit the context of each sentence and picture.
“Do you know what I did last week? No? I got a haircut! What do you think? Let's see what these friends did last weekend. Look at the pictures and help me complete the sentences.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.31 - B. Listen & choose

details: Listen and choose assesses students’ listening comprehension of the unit's key vocabulary and themes. Students listen for specific details to distinguish between two similar pictures and choose the correct one.
Look for focused listening and the ability to correctly identify the picture being described, demonstrated by accurate circling of the corresponding letter.
“Now for our listening challenge! I'm going to play some recordings, but I'm not sure which picture is the right one. I need your expert ears to help me choose correctly.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - A Look and match.

details: Look and match serves as a vocabulary review, connecting activities to locations. Students match the verb phrases to the correct places on the map, reinforcing their understanding of context.
Look for accurately drawn lines that correctly link each activity phrase to its logical location on the town map.
“I have a new map for you! Can you see where everything is? Let's make sure we know where to go for everything. Can you match the activities to the correct places on the map for me? Let’s go!”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.85 - B Read and circle.

details: Read and circle is an assessment of the unit's grammar. Students must choose the correct words in each sentence, demonstrating their understanding of past tense forms and question words.
Look for accurate circling of the correct grammatical forms in all four dialogues, showing a solid understanding of the unit's key grammar points.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.32 - Speaking Our Silly Day! Ask & answer

details: Our Silly Day! is a culminating speaking task that synthesizes the unit's language in a creative, communicative game. Students combine places and actions to create humorous scenarios, encouraging fluent use of the target grammar.

Look for active and enthusiastic participation in the group discussion, confident use of the question and answer forms, and successful completion of the writing task based on their friends' silly answers.

“Let's imagine yesterday was a very silly day! I think I watched a film at the supermarket. That's silly! Let's play a game to create our own silly day stories and find out who had the silliest day of all.”
